title: introduce-hedged-autoscaler-and-burst-fractionation-for-dedicated-fleets
author: Maya Hernandez
release_notes: Adds an opt-in hedged autoscaler mode and a burst fractionation mechanism for Dedicated fleets. Introduces new telemetry metrics for headroom/credit utilization and a set of knobs to tune burst microcredits. No user-facing API breaking changes.
description:
Summary: Implement hedged autoscaler and burst fractionation to improve service continuity and smoother shared burst behavior for Dedicated fleets. Motivation: previously, large tenant microbursts could either exhaust warm pools or force heavy on-demand provisioning spikes. This PR adds a soft-headroom hedging strategy plus a deterministic fractionation algorithm to split burst budgets into smaller microcredits so that warm pools and queueing interact more predictably. The implementation is opt-in via fleet configuration flags (hedge_mode, burst_fractionation_factor) and defaults to off for safety during rollout.

Detailed changes: 1) Autoscaler: new hedged_autoscaler.go implements a soft-headroom model that maintains an anticipatory reserve (fraction of committed capacity plus ephemeral buffer) per-availability-zone. The controller monitors recent allocate/release latencies and computes a hedge score; when hedge_score > threshold the allocator keeps additional warmlets instead of decommitting immediately. New configuration options: hedge_mode=(off|passive|aggressive), hedge_target_percent, hedge_decay_seconds. 2) Burst fractionation: burst_fractionator.go provides deterministic tokenization of tenant burst budgets into microcredits (default size = 5% of tenant burst, configurable via burst_fractionation_factor). Microcredits are accounted separately in the burst ledger and have TTL/aging to avoid long-term accumulation. 3) Metrics & telemetry: add throughput_headroom_p50/p90, burst_fraction_in_flight, microcredit_reuse_rate, credit_age_seconds histograms. These metrics feed the Console dashboard and autoscaler decision logs. 4) Fairness & safety: an updated reservation allocator enforces per-tenant minimum guarantees when fractionation is enabled; a soft-fallback path routes excess microcredits to a spill queue serviced by on-demand pool to avoid hard rejections. 5) Backwards compatibility and migration: feature gate checks added around allocation path; existing reservation files and metrics remain unchanged unless feature enabled. 6) Tests & CI: unit tests for fractionation edge cases, integration test that simulates overlapping bursts across two tenants, and a lightweight e2e canary in perf-canary that ran in the CI job.

Why unique / important: This approach reduces large allocation churn and smooths out headroom consumption spikes by allowing the system to service bursts as a sequence of smaller credits while still preserving tenant guarantees. It also provides richer telemetry to make autoscaler tuning observable.

Risk & rollout plan: default is feature-gated off. Rollout steps: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Enable passive hedge_mode in a single dedicated fleet used for internal load tests; 3) Monitor new telemetry for 48h (throughput_headroom_p90, microcredit_reuse_rate, and credit_age_seconds) and evaluate cost/latency; 4) enable burst_fractionation_factor gradually via canary; 5) optionally move to aggressive mode after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Backout: disable feature flags and drain warmlets; hedged autoscaler intentionally keeps conservative defaults to avoid regressions.

Observability & ops notes: Added traces around allocate/deallocate with a new trace tag "hedge_score" and an allocation_reason enum (scheduled|hedge_hold|microcredit). Console dashboard panels suggested in the PR description (linked in this PR) include per-tenant microcredit usage heatmap and AZ headroom trend.

Configuration examples: fleet.yaml snippet: hedge_mode: passive hedge_target_percent: "8" hedge_decay_seconds: "600" burst_fractionation_factor: "0.05"

Related work: touches autoscaler core (pkg/autoscaler), allocator (pkg/allocator), ledger (pkg/burstledger), and telemetry plumbing (pkg/observability). See Linear ENG-3221 and ENG-3309 for product/engineering requirements.

Files changed (high level): pkg/autoscaler/hedged_autoscaler.go pkg/allocator/burst_fractionator.go pkg/burstledger/ledger_accounting.go pkg/observability/metrics_registry.go config/fleet_defaults.go test/integration/burst_fractionation_test.go test/unit/hedge_score_test.go examples/fleet-hedge.yaml docs/operator/hedge-autoscaler.md CI: added perf-canary job linking to the new test harness.

Commits summary: - initial hedged autoscaler scaffolding and interfaces - fractionation token model and ledger integration - conservative allocation fallback and fairness checks - telemetry hooks, metrics registry entries and Console dashboard suggestions - unit and integration tests + CI job - docs and configuration examples

Merge notes: squashed to a single commit; post-merge follow-ups include a telemetry naming normalization pass and a small refactor of warmlet lifecycle to expose reuse metrics.

review_thread: Aisha: please add a safety net to avoid double-counting microcredits when migrations occur; noted and added (ledger idempotency). Marco: can we bound memory usage for microcredit queue? response: added ttl-based compaction and a fixed memory cap per-tenant. Liang: request clearer metric names and unit tests for credit aging; addressed and expanded tests. Approvals: Aisha approved after idempotency test, Marco approved after memory cap added, Liang approved after metric name change. One CI flaky e2e retried and passed.

operational_playbook: If headroom usage rises >30% on p90 for 1h after enabling passive mode, rollback to previous config and open ENG-RA ticket. For microcredit leak suspicion, monitor credit_age_seconds and run ledger-compact with dry-run to identify stale entries.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated behind fleet config; include operator docs pointer in release notes. Recommend enabling only on non-production fleets in first week.
